newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan cotton prices seen steady, up in India.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan cotton prices seen steady, up in India.

text.p: Cotton prices are likely to remain steady in Pakistan and firm in India in the next week, dealers in the two countries said on Thursday.
Dealers in Karachi said prices held steady in the week to Thursday in dull trade due to Pakistan's elections on February 3 and holidays for the Moslem festival of Eid al-Fitr from Saturday.
"A sharp fall in orders of cotton yarn from abroad due to elections and the Eid holidays has slowed cotton buying by textile mills," dealer Mustafa Hussain said.
But prices were unlikely to fall when the market reopens after Eid on Wednesday as arrivals were slow and availability of quality stocks was low.
In the kerb market, NIAB-78 traded at 2,075 rupees ($51.59) per maund (37.32 kg) and MNH-93 ranged between 2,200 and 2,125.

Thursday Wednesday Jan 30
Indian cotton prices are expected to be firm in the next two to three weeks in anticipation of the government authorising more exports, traders in India said.

They said a decision could come later this month when the Cotton Advisory Board (CAB) in the federal textiles ministry is expected to meet to give final estimates of the 1996/97 crop season ending in September.
"I'm expecting the release of more cotton for export in the next few weeks," said Chandubhai Thakkar, a leading cotton trader.
The CAB recently estimated the 1996/97 crop at 15.50 million bales (170 kg each) compared to the last 16 million-bale crop.
Earlier this week, the government authorised 165,000 bales of exports but the move failed to lift sentiment, Thakkar said.
"Market men were expecting a fresh export quota of about 250,000-300,000 bales," he said.
Since the start of the 1996/97 season four months ago, the government has authorised exports of up to 1.22 million bales compared to 1.5 million in the whole of the previous year.
Traders said the left-leaning United Front coalition was farmer-friendly and wanted to keep domestic prices firm.

Cotton prices held steady in the week to Thursday in Bombay against poor demand from cotton mills despite a drop in arrivals in the northern region, traders said. Arrivals in Punjab remained ow during the week ahead of the assembly elections there.
Spot Bengal-deshi was quiet at 775/825 rupees per maund and Punjab saw-ginned was unchanged at 1,390/1,620. Punjab F-414 was 1,815/1,830 rupees.
Gujarat Kalyan (medium-staple) was quiet at 11,500/11,700 rupees per candy (355.56 kg). Gujarat Sankar-4 (long-staple) was steady at 16,500/17,000 for average variety and 18,000/18,500 for superior.
